summary: Reproduced that all dynamic LoRA handlers permit tokenizer_worker_num > 1 despite per-process registries, then added a deterministic fail-fast guard before backend calls or local mutations. Multi-worker dynamic LoRA synchronization remains unsupported.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: 4 failures showed both load variants succeeding with two tokenizer workers, and unload consulting only the serving worker's empty registry. Raw output: reports/j-55f7d05688e3/raw/pytest_before.log

Passing-after regression and boundaries: all three dynamic APIs reject before backend/state mutation; DP attention does not bypass the guard; single-worker dynamic updates and startup-preloaded registries remain functional. 6 passed. Raw output: reports/j-55f7d05688e3/raw/pytest_after.log
Focused regression plus neighboring LoRA result-merging and multi-tokenizer routing tests. 16 passed. Raw output: reports/j-55f7d05688e3/raw/pytest_related.log
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, and CI registry checks for changed source and test files. Raw output: reports/j-55f7d05688e3/raw/precommit.log

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect and correction are tokenizer-process control-plane behavior. The deterministic reproduction used the actual handlers and registry with mocked backend communication; no GPU command was run.

remaining_limitations: This correction rejects unsupported multi-tokenizer dynamic updates; it does not synchronize LoRA state across tokenizer workers.
No model weights or full HTTP serving reproduction were used, so real-model transport, architecture semantics, and distributed execution remain unverified.
The assigned gfx950 GPU was not used because no numerical kernel or model-execution claim is made.
